items.title: SpaceX's Starship faces 5-month launch gap as IPO filing nears

featured_image.name: SpaceX's major Starship test delayed after technical issue

items.description:
SpaceX has gone nearly five months without a Starship launch — the longest pause since the program's early days — even as the company prepares to file paperwork for what could become the largest initial public offering in history.

The world's largest rocket last flew on October 13, 2025, when Flight 11 closed out a year of five test missions. As of early March, no official launch date has been set for Flight 12, and the mission does not appear on SpaceX's online schedule. Elon Musk suggested in a January 26 post on X that the next launch was six weeks away, pointing to a March liftoff, but that timeline has not been confirmed by the company.[1][2][3]

items.title: Apple unveils six devices in two days, more expected

featured_image.name: Apple MacBook Pro M5 14-inch review: A huge graphics ...

items.description:
Apple has announced six new products over two days in its most aggressive spring launch in years, with at least one more device expected when the company hosts media at a hands-on "experience" event on Wednesday.

The announcements began Monday, March 2, with the iPhone 17e and the M4 iPad Air, followed Tuesday by the M5 MacBook Air, M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro, and a pair of new Studio Displays. Pre-orders for most of the new hardware open March 4, with availability beginning March 11.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Dow sinks as oil surges on Iran's Strait of Hormuz shutdown

featured_image.name: Iran partially closes Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil choke point, as Tehran holds talks with U.S.

items.description:
Oil prices soared for a third consecutive day on Tuesday and stocks tumbled sharply as the war between the United States and Iran entered its fourth day, with tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz at a near standstill and no signs of a quick resolution to the conflict.

West Texas Intermediate crude climbed roughly 8% to around $76.91 per barrel, while Brent crude jumped about 7.6% to $83.65, its highest level since mid-2024, according to CNN. The Dow Jones Industrial Average sank more than 1,000 points in early trading, while the S&P 500 fell over 2% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped by a similar margin.[1][2][3]

items.title: Dow drops over 1,000 points as Iran conflict roils markets

featured_image.name: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures plunge as fresh strikes intensify Iran conflict

items.description:
A wave of selling swept through global equity markets on Monday and Tuesday as the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran entered its fourth day with no sign of de-escalation, rattling investors with fears of prolonged energy disruption and a fresh surge in inflation.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged more than 1,000 points on Tuesday, March 3 — on pace for its largest single-day drop since April 2025, according to The Wall Street Journal. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.5% and 1.9%, respectively, in pre-market trading Tuesday. A day earlier, U.S. stocks had staged a late-session recovery, with the S&P 500 finishing nearly flat and the Nasdaq Composite gaining 0.4%, after initially dropping more than 1%.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump open to arming militias inside Iran, officials say

featured_image.name: Scoop: Trump calls Kurdish leaders in Iran war effort

items.description:
President Trump is open to backing armed groups inside Iran willing to fight the Islamic regime, U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal on Monday, a move that would deepen American involvement in a conflict that has already killed Iran's supreme leader and drawn the U.S. into its largest Middle Eastern military operation in two decades.[1]

The revelation came as Trump spoke by phone on Sunday with the leaders of Iraq's two main Kurdish factions — Masoud Barzani and Bafel Talabani — to discuss the war and what might come next, according to Axios, which first reported the calls. Kurdish forces maintain thousands of troops along the Iran-Iraq border and have deep ties with Iran's Kurdish minority. The outreach was driven in part by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has long cultivated relationships with Kurdish groups and raised their potential role during a meeting with Trump at the White House, Axios reported.[2][3]

items.title: IAEA says no nuclear sites hit in Iran strikes as Tehran alleges Natanz was targeted

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Iran dramatically accelerating uranium enrichment ...

items.description:
The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency told an emergency board meeting on Monday that the agency has found no evidence Iran is developing nuclear weapons, even as he warned that ongoing U.S. and Israeli military strikes risk triggering a radiological disaster.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi addressed the agency's 35-nation Board of Governors in Vienna on March 2, convened at Russia's request following the launch of Operation Roaring Lion — a coordinated U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran that began on February 28. Grossi told the board that the IAEA has "no indication" that any nuclear installations in Iran, "including the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant, the Tehran Research Reactor, or other nuclear fuel cycle facilities have been damaged or hit".[1][2][3]

items.title: Hardy bacterium survives Mars-like asteroid blast in lab

featured_image.name: Asteroid Impacts Could Launch Living Microbes From Mars

items.description:
A resilient desert bacterium survived pressures equivalent to being blasted off the surface of Mars by an asteroid strike, according to a new study from Johns Hopkins University, lending fresh support to the idea that life could travel between planets aboard space debris.

The research, published Monday in PNAS Nexus, found that the extremophile Deinococcus radiodurans — a bacterium found in the high deserts of Chile — achieved nearly 100% survival at 1.4 Gigapascals of pressure and 60% survival at 2.4 Gigapascals, far exceeding what scientists had thought possible. By comparison, other commonly studied microorganisms such as E. coli and Shewanella oneidensis showed survival rates below 10% at similar pressures.[1][2]

items.title: Israel sends ground forces into southern Lebanon amid Hezbollah clashes
items.description:
Israeli troops crossed into southern Lebanon on Tuesday, seizing new positions beyond the border as the military expanded its campaign against Hezbollah following days of rocket and drone attacks that have opened a second front in the broader U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

The Israel Defense Forces said soldiers from the 91st "Galilee" Division entered southern Lebanon and captured several strategic points as part of what the military called an "enhanced forward defense posture," moving beyond five outposts Israel has maintained since a ceasefire was reached in November 2024. Eyewitnesses told Xinhua that an Israeli force including a tank and three military bulldozers crossed the Blue Line at around 8:00 a.m. local time, advancing roughly one kilometer into Lebanese territory near the town of Tal al-Nahas.[1][2][3]
